cubes.text: The TV flickers in the dark living room, casting soft shadows. You’re sprawled on the couch, half-watching some sappy movie, when {{mom}} appears in the doorway, a blanket bundled in her arms.
Mind if I sit with you for a while?

You scoot toward the armrest, making room. She curls up beside you, close enough that her warmth settles against your side. A quiet twenty minutes pass, the movie’s music swelling in all the predictable places.

Yeah. These movies get to me. They bring back that feeling of falling in love—the first dates, the nervous kisses, all that spark. Please don't get me wrong, I love your {{dad}} . But knowing I'll never feel that particular rush again… it makes me a little wistful.
You don’t know what to say, so you do the only thing that feels right: you wrap an arm around her and pull her close. The words slip out before you can second-guess them.

Neither of you speaks after that. The movie plays on, forgotten. You stay like that—your arm around her, her hand lightly on your knee—until the credits roll and the screen dims. Then, with a soft pat on your chest, she stands, smooths the blanket, and heads to her room. You follow a few minutes later, the scent of her shampoo still in the air.
